Hi Sophie / Marcus — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary workload: batched inference for clinical triage model (avg seq len ~256, 99% requests < 500 tokens).
- Peak predictable traffic window: 08:00–12:00 PT, 600 TPS peak during batch windows; steady-state ~80 TPS otherwise.
- Data/security needs: PHI in payloads, require VPC private deployment or Dedicated with strict isolation + KMS integration.
- Business goals: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for inference with 5–10ms 95th token latency target for short responses; cost per 1k tokens must be predictable for budgeting.

Redwood’s recommended approach (high-level)
- Reserved Dedicated pool: 8-GPU initial commit (NVIDIA A100-class equivalent), isolated tenancy (single-tenant pool) with optional on-prem connector if you need full air-gap later.
- Autoscaling/burst: keep baseline steady capacity with burst policy to add up to 12 GPUs during peak windows.
- Ops & SLA: 99.9% compute availability, with runbook for fallbacks to a lower-cost compatible model variant if we detect saturation.

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a one-page mutual action plan and a draft SLA (see attachments). Please review the SLA section on maintenance windows and latency SLOs.
2) Sophie — can you share the contact for procurement and your security reviewer so we can send the SOC2/infra evidence?
3) Ben (cc’d) will follow up with a brief ops note describing isolation options and KMS flow.
4) We’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) to validate throughput numbers and perf targets. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Do you need dedicated network egress (fixed IPs) or can you route through our managed egress?
- Are there any regulatory approvals that mandate on-prem?

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your procurement timeline.

Best,

Hi Sophie — quick ops note to address the isolation / perf questions raised: 

Isolation options (short)- Single-tenant Dedicated pool: physical tenancy isolation at the pool level, dedicated CUDA contexts per tenant, network namespaces per allocation. This prevents other customers from sharing GPUs in the pool.
- Multi-tenant with soft isolation: workload pinning + quotas (cheaper but less strict).

Noisy-neighbor protections- We provide persistent GPU reservation per allocation and CPU pinning for companion processes; burst nodes are separate from baseline nodes to avoid cross-impact.
- Network: we can configure VLAN-segmented egress and per-subnet rate limits.
- Storage IOPS: we recommend attached NVMe for your batch windows; we can size to 10–20 GB/s depending on model weight.

SLA + maintenance- We can accommodate a 2-hour quarterly maintenance window in the draft SLA; outside of that we commit to 99.9% monthly availability for compute. Tiered credits are included in the SLA doc.

Sizing & perf assumptions (for cost est)
- Baseline 8 x A100-class GPUs -> target 80–120 qps for small prompt paths, burst to 12 GPUs -> headroom for 600 TPS during parallel batch windows depending on batching configuration.
- We'll run a perf test during the technical deep-dive to validate these numbers; recommend keeping a 20% buffer for headroom.

Next technical step
- Proposed deep-dive agenda: perf expectations, KV cache strategy, quantization options, networking requirements, and perf test schedule.

I’ve attached the short MAP and the SLA draft to Sean’s original email — happy to jump on the deep-dive with you next week.

Thanks,
